question: A scooterist is travelling at the speed of 42 km/h. How much distance (in km) will they travel in 90 minutes?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Distance is the product of speed and time.

Time in hours = 90 ÷ 60 = 1.5 hours.

Distance = 42 × 1.5 = 63 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 63 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of the scooterist = 42 km/h

Time taken = 90 minutes

 
• 
 
 
 Start
 End
 
 
 Speed = 42 km/h
 Time = 1.5 h
 
 

 
 

 Distance = 63 km

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, we convert the time from minutes to hours because the speed is in km/h.

⇒ Time = 90 ÷ 60 hours

⇒ Time = 1.5 hours

⇒ Distance = 42 × 1.5

⇒ Distance = 63 km

**∴ The correct answer is 63 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5 ÷ 18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.

Average Speed

When identical distances are covered at speeds S₁ and S₂, Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed

For bodies moving in the same direction, Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|. For bodies moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.
